findings.title: Empty <set> yields an UPDATE without assignments
findings.description: When every <if> guard in the <set> block evaluates false, the emitted SQL becomes 'UPDATE COMPANY WHERE ID = ?' with no SET clause. Whether the target DBMS treats this as a no-op or as a syntax error is DBMS-dependent and was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Ensure at least one updatable column is non-null before invocation, or handle the empty-<set> case explicitly so the emitted SQL always carries a SET clause.

findings.title: No optimistic-locking predicate
findings.description: The WHERE clause contains only ID; there is no version or update-time check, so concurrent updates last-write-wins without lost-update detection.
findings.recommendation: Add a version or update_time condition to the WHERE clause and return the affected-row count to detect concurrent modification.

findings.title: Null id silently matches zero rows
findings.description: If the caller passes a null id, 'ID = NULL' is never true under standard SQL semantics and the update silently affects zero rows.
findings.recommendation: Validate that id is non-null before invocation and treat a zero affected-row result as an error condition.

findings.title: No update-time metadata column maintained
findings.description: The assignment list does not maintain any updated_at/update_time metadata column, so audit-trail and schema-drift risks exist.
findings.recommendation: Consider maintaining an update_time column and deriving the assignment list from the mapped entity to avoid hard-coded column drift.
